The void-free blind microvia copper electroplating process is a key technology in HDI PCB manufacturing. This work systematically studied the influence of the Acid Blue 1 (AB1) leveler on blind microvia filling. AB1 exhibits excellent suppression during electroplating, with its efect strengthening as the AB1 concentration increases. Chronopotentiometry was used to study the interaction among AB1, SPS, and PEG. There is a synergistic suppressing interaction between the new leveler AB1 and suppressor PEG, while there is competition between AB1 and accelerator SPS. During electrodeposition, AB1 can adsorb on the copper substrate to reduce active sites and suppress copper electrodeposition, based on theoretical studies and in situ infrared spectroscopy. At the optimized electroplating process, void-free microvia filling is achieved with 20 mg L<sup>-1</sup> AB1 and successive electroplating confirms the stability of AB1. Based on difusion diferences among additives and the competition between AB1 and SPS, a gradient competitive adsorption superfilling mechanism was proposed to illustrate the filling process of the AB1–SPS–PEG system. AB1 is beneficial to improving flatness and lowering surface roughness of the copper layer, which is conducive to reducing signal losses during high-frequency transmission. Additionally, AB1 can modulate the preferential formation of Cu(111) and Cu(200) and facilitate grain refinement.

Copper is widely used as an interconnect line in blind microvias for PCB manufacturing due to its good electronic (thermal and electrical conductivity) and mechanical (wear resistance and elongation, etc.) properties.<sup>6,7</sup> The filling of blind microvias with copper is achieved through electroplating technology.<sup>8–10</sup> In PCBs, copper not only provides a stable electrical connection but also enhances the structural strength of HDI PCBs, improving heat and wear resistance.<sup>11</sup> Moreover, copper interconnect lines effectively reduce losses in signal transmission and enhance signal integrity, which is especially important for high-frequency and high-speed circuits.<sup>12</sup> During copper electroplating, it is essential to adjust the metal deposition process in local microvias to avoid the formation of void defects caused by the edge effect, which can undermine the properties of the copper interconnect layer. The most common method is the addition of proper additives.<sup>13–15</sup>

The additives used in copper electroplating fall into three categories: accelerators, suppressors, and levelers.<sup>16</sup> The most commonly used accelerator, suppressor, and leveler is bis-(sodium sulfopropyl)- disulfide (SPS), polyethylene glycol (PEG), and Janus Green B (JGB).<sup>17</sup> During electroplating, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) studies reveal that the disulfide bond of SPS will break up, with the sulfurcontaining side adsorbing on the copper base, while the other side (containing a sulfonic acid group) captures free $\operatorname { C u } ^ { 2 + }$ to accelerate reduction with adsorbed Cl<sup>-</sup> through the ‘‘bridging efect’’.<sup>18–20</sup> As for PEG, in situ Raman and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations confirm the formation of $\mathbf { P E G - C u ^ { 2 + } - C l ^ { - } }$ adsorbate complexes, which increase the energy barrier and suppress copper electrodeposition.<sup>21–23</sup> Mass spectrometry (MS) and DFT calculations demonstrate that the azo group of JGB competes with the reduction of $\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 + }$ to obtain electrons, leading to dissociation<sup>24,25</sup> into phenazine derivatives that can also adsorb on active sites to suppress copper growth.<sup>26,27</sup> Among these additives, levelers are key components for achieving defect-free filling in blind vias.<sup>28</sup> Nowadays, triphenylmethane derivatives are promising levelers and have been used in throughhole and blind-hole filling due to the unlocalized orbital distribution of the tertiary amine structure.<sup>29,30</sup>

In electroplating experiments, phosphor copper plates $( 5 \times 1 0 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } )$ were used as the anode, while PCB plates $( 5 \times 1 0 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } )$ served as the cathode. Gas pumping, with a rate of 20 L h<sup>-1</sup>, was employed to stir the solution and accelerate mass transfer during electroplating. Each electroplating used 1.5 L solution, with the solution composition and optimized values shown in Table 1. Before electroplating, the PCB was cleaned with acetone and activated using 10 wt% $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { S O } _ { 4 } .$ . The electroplating time for filling microvias was 3 h.

3.1.3 Chronopotentiometry analysis. It is important to study the interaction among SPS (accelerator), PEG (suppressor), and AB1 (leveler), as it provides a deeper understanding of the filling mechanism in microvias.<sup>45</sup> Traditionally, galvanostatic measurement is applied to study possible interactions by changing the injection order of the three types of additives. Fig. 1c (up) shows the change in cathodic potential after injecting additives into the testing solution. The cathodic potential declines (230 mV) after adding PEG, indicating its suppressing efect. Upon introducing AB1, the cathodic potential further decreases (31 mV), suggesting synergistic cooperation between AB1 and PEG. However, after the addition of SPS, the cathodic potential shifts positively (42 mV), indicating the accelerating efect of SPS in the presence of AB1 and PEG. By altering the additive injection order, SPS can cause a positive shift of 205 mV in cathodic potential after PEG injection, suggesting that SPS can replace PEG to accelerate copper electrodeposition, consistent with previous work.<sup>46</sup> Following AB1 injection, the cathodic potential changes negatively (-191 mV). Additionally, the potential reaches the same level regardless of injection order, further verifying the competition between SPS and AB1. Fig. 1c (down) provides a schematic diagram illustrating the relationships among SPS, PEG, and AB1, showing cooperation between AB1 and PEG, but competition between AB1 and SPS.

3.3.1 Electroplating performance. The optimization of the electroplating process is shown in Fig. 3, with the used devices illustrated in Fig. 3c. Without AB1, the growth rate at the opening area is higher than that at the bottom and side walls, leading to void defects in microvias with both diameters (125 mm and 150 mm). At an AB1 concentration of 10 mg ${ { \bf L } ^ { - 1 } } ,$ the growth rate at the opening area decreases due to AB1 adsorption, which suppresses copper growth. However, this relatively low concentration is not conducive to establishing an efective concentration gradient, resulting in defects forming in the 125 mm microvias and concave growth in the 150 mm microvias. With 20 mg $\mathrm { ~ L ~ } ^ { - 1 } \ \mathbf { A B 1 }$ , an efective concentration gradient is formed, allowing copper to grow from bottom to top without defects in either microvias. Besides, the compact and flat copper morphology from the top view in Fig. S4 (ESI†) indicates that AB1 improves copper quality compared to layers obtained without it. In contrast, the commonly used leveler Janus Green B (Fig. S5, ESI†) produces a copper layer that contains gas holes, despite yielding a flat and defect-free surface, demonstrating that AB1 is superior in enhancing copper quality. The influence of morphology will be discussed in Section 3.4.1. When the AB1 concentration increases further to $3 0 \mathrm { m g L } ^ { - 1 }$ , the excessive concentration weakens the concentration gradient, causing the bottom-up growth mode to shift to a conformal growth mode in the 150 mm microvias. Overall, 20 mg L<sup>-1</sup> AB1 is determined to be optimum.

3.3.2 Filling mechanism. The difusion property of AB1 was studied using molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, as shown in Fig. S8 (ESI†). Based on the Einstein equation (eqn (S2), ESI†), the difusion coeficient for AB1 $\left( D _ { \mathbf { A B 1 } } \right)$ is 2  $1 0 ^ { - 1 0 } \mathrm { m } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ , which is close to the difusion coeficient for PEG $\left( D _ { \mathrm { P E G } } , 1 \times 1 0 ^ { - 1 0 } \mathrm { m } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 } \right) ^ { 5 0 }$ and one order smaller than that for SPS $\big ( D _ { \mathrm { S P S } } , 5 \times 1 0 ^ { - 9 } \mathrm { ~ m } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { ~ s } ^ { - 1 } \big ) . ^ { 5 1 }$ This illustrates that the leveler AB1 and suppressor PEG have slower difusion transport compared to the accelerator SPS. Coupled with the interactions among the three additives discussed in Section 3.1.3, namely the competition between AB1 and SPS, as well as cooperation between AB1 and PEG, gradient competitive adsorption superfilling was proposed to illustrate the AB1–SPS–PEG system, with a schematic diagram shown in Fig. 3d. At the initial stage (3d1), different additives are distributed uniformly within the microvias. As the filling process progresses (3d2), a concentration gradient for the additives forms due to their consumption and local diffusion transport limitations within the microvias. However, the concentration ratio of SPS to PEG and AB1 at the bottom increases compared to that at the opening area due to the differing diffusion properties among the three additives; specifically, $D _ { \mathrm { S P S } }$ is significantly larger than $D _ { \mathbf { A B 1 } }$ and $D _ { \mathbf { P E G } } .$ . As a result, the growth rate at the bottom is improved by the increased accelerating effect from the relatively amount of SPS, while growth at the opening area is effectively suppressed since AB1’s mass transport is not limited due to convection, leading to copper growth from the bottom to the top. At the final stage (3d3), the three additives redistribute uniformly at the opening area, resulting in the same growth rate across different areas. No momentum plating phenomena occur in the AB1–SPS–PEG system.<sup>52</sup>

3.4.1 Efect of AB1 on morphology. Fig. 4 and 5a show the surface morphology of the copper layer observed by SEM and Olympus conformal laser microscope.<sup>53</sup> Small bump particles are present on the uneven copper surface electrodeposited without AB1. After introducing 10 mg $\mathrm { L } ^ { - 1 }$ AB1, the surface flatness improves greatly, and the copper layer becomes compact, although large bump morphology remains. As the AB1 concentration continues to rise, the flatness of the copper layer further improves. Using the Olympus conformal laser microscope, the surface roughness $\left( R _ { \mathrm { z } } \right)$ was calculated, as shown in Fig. 5b. $R _ { \mathrm { z } }$ is 128 nm for the copper layer obtained without AB1 and decreases to 92 nm with 10 mg $\mathrm { L } ^ { - 1 }$ AB1. Furthermore, $R _ { \mathrm { z } }$ values obtained from 20 mg $\mathrm { L } ^ { - 1 }$ and 30 mg $\mathrm { L } ^ { - 1 }$ are 83 nm and 75 nm, respectively. The above analysis indicates that AB1 has a micro-scale leveling efect.

3.4.2 Efect of AB1 on signal loss. The influence of AB1 on signal loss during high-frequency transmission was studied using finite element simulation.<sup>54</sup> Fig. 5c shows that signal loss is influenced by surface roughness and applied frequency. Total loss increases with rising frequency and $R _ { \mathrm { z } } .$ Additionally, the total loss with frequency for the copper layer obtained with JGB is also calculated (Fig. S5d, ESI†). In comparison, the signal loss obtained with AB1 is smaller than with JGB at the same frequency due to a lower $R _ { \mathrm { z } }$ for AB1. The skin efect for the optimized copper layer with 20 mg $\mathrm { L } ^ { - 1 }$ AB1 and without AB1 is shown in Fig. 5d and e. At a relatively low frequency (10 GHz), current density is distributed uniformly in the copper layer obtained from $2 0 \mathrm { m g L } ^ { - 1 }$ . Even at high frequency (100 GHz), the current density remains relatively well distributed. However, for the copper layer obtained without AB1, the current density mainly concentrates near the surface area at 10 GHz. Simulation results indicate that AB1 helps mitigate the influence of the skin efect during high-frequency signal transmission by improving surface flatness.

A novel leveler, Acid Blue 1, was used to achieve void-free copper filling in blind microvias. Electrochemical tests (CV and EIS) confirm the suppressive efect on the reduction of $\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 + }$ . During copper electroplating, there is a synergistic suppression between AB1 and PEG, but competition between AB1 and SPS. DFT calculations and in situ infrared spectroscopy provide a deeper understanding of AB1 adsorption configuration on the copper substrate during electrodeposition, indicating that AB1 can reduce active sites and act as a barrier adsorption layer to increase cathodic polarization. After electroplating optimization, microvias with diameters of 125 mm and 150 mm can be filled with 20 mg $\mathrm { L } ^ { - 1 }$ AB1 at $1 . 5 \mathrm { A } \mathrm { d } \mathrm { m } ^ { - 2 } ;$ the good stability of AB1 indicates its industrial potential. A gradient competitive adsorption superfilling mechanism was proposed to explain the filling process for the AB1–SPS–PEG system. The diffusion differences among the three additives and the competition between AB1 and SPS are key to achieving bottom-up growth in microvias. AB1 improves the copper layer quality, enhances surface flatness, refines the grains, and reduces signal losses during high-frequency transmission. Additionally, AB1 suppresses the formation of Cu(220) while promoting the formation of Cu(111) and Cu(200).

ABSTRACT: Driven by the rapid development of 5G/6G communications, high-performance computing, and artificial intelligence, the metallization of high-aspect-ratio through-holes (THs) in printed circuit boards (PCBs) imposes stringent requirements on the thickness uniformity and interconnect reliability of electroplated copper layers. This study systematically investigates the application of a novel leveler, thiazolyl blue (MTT), for PCB THs’ electroplating, successfully realizing high-quality conformal deposition in high-aspect-ratio (10:1) THs. Electrochemical analyses demonstrate that MTT significantly enhances the cathodic polarization and efectively inhibits the reduction of Cu<sup>2+</sup>. Meanwhile, microscopic morphological characterizations confirm

that MTT exhibits excellent leveling capability, reducing the surface roughness of the copper deposit to as low as 0.147 μm. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the high inhibitory eficiency of MTT originates from the dominant interfacial adsorption of MTT at the cathode. with the bulk cation-π interaction with $\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 + }$ contributing as a minor secondary effect at the microscopic level. Crystallographic and interfacial wettability analyses further indicate that MTT effectively refines the grain size and promotes the preferential growth of the Cu(200) plane while improving the wettability of the plating bath. In practical high-aspect-ratio through-hole plating tests, the introduction of MTT substantially increases the throwing power (TP) from 25.2% to 96.8%. Based on these results, a competitive interfacial polarization remodeling mechanism governed by multiphysics coupling is proposed to elucidate the intrinsic role of MTT in promoting conformal through-hole deposition. This work provides a solid theoretical foundation and practical engineering guidance for the fabrication of highly reliable, high-frequency 3D interconnected PCB structures.

Driven by the rapid advancement of 5G/6G communications, high-performance computing, and artificial intelligence (AI), printed circuit boards (PCBs)�the mother of electronic products�are undergoing profound technological revolutions.<sup>1−3</sup> As the fundamental carrier connecting electronic components, the PCB not only provides mechanical support for chips and passive devices but also functions as the neural network sustaining signal transmission and power delivery throughout the electronic system.<sup>4</sup> With the accelerated evolution of PCBs toward high integration, high interconnect density, and high-frequency/high-speed transmission, this trajectory poses two intertwined materials challenges. On the device side, the suppression of electromagnetic interference, interlayer crosstalk, and thermal accumulation in densely packed high-frequency boards has stimulated intensive research into advanced electromagnetic functional materials, with MXene-based two-dimensional absorbers and heterostructured composites emerging as a particularly promising family that delivers eficient GHz-to-THz electromagnetic wave absorption and integrated thermal management.<sup>5−8</sup> On the interconnect side, the multilayer copper network that mechanically and electrically links the chips must, in parallel, be reformulated to simultaneously sustain signal integrity, ensure robust interconnect reliability, and guarantee long-term service lifespan under increasingly aggressive high-frequency operation�demands that ultimately translate into unprece dentedly stringent requirements on the copper metallization of microvias with high aspect ratios. Copper electrodeposition in high-aspect-ratio through-holes (THs) is the core technology for achieving interlayer electrical interconnection in multilayer PCBs. The quality of this metallization directly dictates the signal integrity, current-carrying capacity, and long-term service lifespan of the electronic devices.<sup>9,10</sup>

However, during the practical electroplating of high-aspect ratio THs, the initial current distribution is highly nonuniform due to geometric constraints. The local current density at the via opening is significantly higher than that at the center, accompanied by severe mass transfer limitations of Cu<sup>2+</sup> within the hole. This multiphysics imbalance frequently triggers the “dog-bone” defect, characterized by excessive copper accumulation at the via opening and excessively thin deposits on the inner walls.<sup>11</sup> Such nonuniform deposition severely compromises the electrical and mechanical performance of the interconnected structures, constituting a universal bottleneck in the high-density interconnect (HDI) industry.<sup>12</sup> To overcome this challenge, it is imperative to introduce suppressors, accelerators, and levelers into the acidic copper sulfate bath.<sup>13</sup> The precise synergistic and competitive adsorption among these three additives dynamically modulates the deposition kinetics at diferent spatial locations within the TH, ultimately achieving high-quality conformal interconnection.

Typically, polyether macromolecules (e.g., polyethylene glycol, PEG) serve as suppressors; bridged by chloride ions, they profoundly enhance cathodic polarization and retard copper growth.<sup>14</sup> Sulfonate compounds bearing thiol or disulfide groups (e.g., bis(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide, SPS) act as accelerators: they capture Cu<sup>2+</sup> at the cathode interface and lower the activation barrier for its reduction.<sup>15</sup> Among the plating formulations, the leveler plays the most critica interfacial regulatory role. By preferentially adsorbing at strongly convected regions (e.g., the opening), the leveler establishes a localized high-impedance barrier that inhibits overplating,<sup>16−18</sup> thereby compelling the spatial electric field lines to redistribute deeper into TH.<sup>19−21</sup> To date, various commercial dyes have been reported as levelers (e.g., Janus Green B, tetrazolium blue chloride, PAN).<sup>22−24</sup> Meanwhile, some researchers have devoted eforts to the synthesis of nove polymeric levelers (e.g., VIBDGE, PBDGE, Sudan-QNL). 25−27 Nevertheless, each of the aforementioned levelers exhibits specific limitations. Polymeric levelers such as VIBDGE and PBDGE, despite their promising performance, typically require multistep synthesis and tedious purification procedures, which considerably increase the production cost and hinder their practical scalability. Commercial dye-based levelers (e.g., Janus Green B) are readily accessible and have been widely adopted in industry with proven efectiveness; however, as the aspec ratio of through-holes continues to increase, further enhance ment of throwing power remains highly desirable to ensure the thickness uniformity and long-term reliability of the copper interconnects. In this regard, MTT ofers a compelling combination of advantages: it is a commercially available, of the-shelf reagent that can be directly procured at low cost entirely eliminating the need for custom synthesis or purification, and as will be demonstrated in Section 3.5, it delivers a throwing power (TP = 96.8%) that markedly outperforms the conventional leveler JGB (TP = 84.5%) under identical bath composition and process conditions. Therefore, a systematic investigation of MTT as a tailored leveler for high aspect-ratio PCB through-hole electroplating is of urgent practical significance.

All chemical reagents employed in this work, including copper sulfate pentahydrate $( \mathrm { \check { C } } \mathrm { u } \mathrm { S O } _ { 4 } { \cdot } 5 \mathrm { \check { H } } _ { 2 } \mathrm { \check { O } } )$ and sulfuric acid $\mathrm { ( H } _ { 2 } \bar { \mathrm { S O } } _ { 4 } ,$ 98 wt %), were purchased from Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Co., Ltd., China. The accelerator bis(sodium sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS, CAS No. 27206-35-5), the suppressor polyethylene glycol (PEG, molecular weight = 20,000, CAS No. 25322-68-3), and the leveler Thiazolyl Blue (MTT, 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium, CAS No. 298-93-1) were all purchased from Shanghai Aladdin Biochemical Technology $\mathrm { C o . , L t \hat { d } . }$ , China. All chemicals used were of analytical grade purity (AR) and applied without any further purification process, and all test aqueous solutions were prepared using deionized water.

The microstructure of the electrodeposited copper layers was systematically characterized via multidimensional analytical approaches. A field-emission scanning electron microscope (Zeiss Supra55, Germany) was utilized to observe the surface morphology under an acceleration voltage of 5 kV. The surface roughness parameter (Sa) was quantitatively analyzed using an ultra-depth-of field 3D microscope (Olympus DSX510), and the average roughness (Sa) of each sample was calculated as the mean value of measurements obtained from three diferent regions. X-ray difraction (XRD, Bruker D8) was employed to investigate the preferential crystal plane orientation of the electrodeposited copper layers, and the measurements were performed at a voltage of 40 kV and a current of 40 mA, with continuous scanning at a rate of $0 . 0 2 ^ { \circ } / s$ over a 2θ range of 20−90°. An optical contact angle meter (Dataphysics-OCA20) was adopted to evaluate the interfacial properties, where 4 μL droplets were used for each test, and the average value was obtained from measurements conducted at five diferent positions.

Cyclic voltammetry (CV) is widely employed to preliminarily evaluate the inhibitive eficacy of additives during electrodeposition.<sup>42</sup> As illustrated in Figure 2a, the cathodic onset potential for copper deposition in the virgin makeup solution (VMS) without MTT is approximately −0.43 V. In contrast, the introduction of merely 20 mg/L MTT significantly intensifies the cathodic polarization, causing the onset potential to shift negatively to −0.61 V. With a further increase in MTT concentration, the cathodic overpotential continues to escalate; when the MTT concentration reaches 60 $\mathrm { { m g / L } , }$ the onset potential further decreases to −0.67 V. This evolutionary trend is highly consistent with the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) results in Figure 1c, robustly confirming that MTT exerts a severe suppressing efect on the copper electrodeposition process. Notably, once the MTT concen tration is increased to 50 mg/L, the increment in overpotential driven by concentration elevation approaches saturation, indicating that the surface adsorption and the corresponding inhibitive efect of MTT have been maximized. Furthermore, the charge density derived from the integrated area of the anodic stripping peak in the CV curves can be employed as a reliable indicator for the quantitative assessment of the inhibition performance of MTT. Figure 2b reveals that the anodic stripping coulomb of VMS is $1 2 1 . 8 6 ~ \mathrm { C } / \mathrm { d m } ^ { 2 }$ , which drastically decreases to $9 1 . 3 7 ~ \mathrm { C } / \mathrm { d } \mathrm { m } ^ { 2 }$ upon the addition of 20 mg/L MTT. When the concentration is elevated to 60 mg/L, the stripping coulomb plummets to $3 2 . 6 2 { \mathrm { C } } / { \mathrm { d m } } ^ { 2 } ,$ representing a 73.2% reduction compared to that of VMS. This remarkable decrease in anodic stripping coulomb further corroborates the profound suppression of copper deposition induced by MTT.<sup>43,44</sup>

The potential diference $( \Delta \eta )$ between 100 and 1000 rpm under various MTT concentrations can be calculated to evaluate the microvia filling performance; typically, a larger $\Delta \eta$ is more conducive to achieving excellent superfilling. Figure 2g demonstrates that as the MTT concentration increases from 20 mg/L to 50 mg/L, Δη broadens significantly from 3.4 mV to 19.3 mV. However, with a further increase in MTT concentration, Δη follows a descending trend. The relatively high Δη values maintained within the concentration window of 40−50 mg/L suggest that this range is optimal for the conformal filling of through-holes. It is noteworthy that the $\Delta \eta$ values obtained from the CP measurements are well correlated with the actual through-hole filling results. A larger Δη signifies a greater polarization disparity between the high-convection region (hole opening) and the low-convection region (hole center), which serves as the electrochemical driving force for redistributing the deposition current toward the hole interior.<sup>16,30,47</sup> The optimal $\Delta \eta$ window of 40−50 mg/L coincides precisely with the MTT concentration that yields the highest throwing power (TP = 96.8% at 50 mg/L, as will be shown in Section 3.5), thereby confirming the predictive validity of the CP-based evaluation for through-hole filling performance. Additionally, chronopotentiometry is frequently utilized to probe the synergistic or competitive interactions among multicomponent additives in the plating bath. By altering the injection sequence of the three core additives, the dynamic interactive mechanisms among MTT, bis(3-sulfopropyl)-disulfide (SPS), and polyethylene glycol (PEG) were systematically analyzed. As delineated by the blue line in Figure 2h, the sequential introduction of SPS and MTT into a system predosed with PEG triggers intense depolarization (a positive shift of 165.8 mV) and polarization (a negative shift of 149.6 mV) responses, respectively. This demonstrates that MTT and the accelerator SPS undergo competitive adsorption on the cathode surface, thereby jointly regulating the electrodeposition morphology of copper.
## 3.3. Theoretical Insights into the Inhibition Mechanism

In this section, Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were conducted to unravel the interfacial adsorption and coordination efects of MTT during copper electrodeposition, thereby systematically elucidating its inhibition mechanism at the microscopic scale. The optimized geometric configuration of the MTT molecule is depicted in Figure S3. Frontier Molecular Orbital theory is extensively employed to analyze and predict the interfacial adsorption behavior of molecules. As illustrated in Figure 3a, the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) are predominantly localized on the tetrazole and thiazole rings, indicating that these functional groups serve as active centers for preferential adsorption.<sup>10,48</sup> Furthermore, the surface electrostatic potential distribution histogram (Figure 3c) reveals that the overall MTT molecule is positively charged,<sup>49,50</sup> possessing a remarkably high average surface electrostatic potential of 65.23 kcal/mol. Driven by robust electrostatic attraction during the electrodeposition process, MTT is highly prone to adsorbing onto the cathodic surface, thereby efectively suppressing copper reduction. To further probe the interfacial adsorption dynamics of MTT on the copper substrate, charge density diference calculations were performed to quantitatively assess its adsorption behavior (Figure 3d and e). The pronounced interfacial charge redistribution between the copper substrate and the MTT molecule decisively confirms their close geometric proximity and intense electronic interaction. Further thermodynamic calculations yield a highly negative adsorption energy $\mathrm { o f } - 2 . 9 3$ eV. This value is consistent with�and slightly more conservative than�the magnitude reported for MTT on Cu(111) under an essentially equivalent level of theory (PBE + Grimme D3 dispersion, slab calculation: $E _ { \mathrm { a d s } } \approx - 8 . 1 4 \ \mathrm { e V } ;$ −785.93 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>) by Yang et $\mathrm { a l . , } ^ { 2 9 }$ confirming that the strong MTT−Cu(111) interfacial adsorption is robustly captured by the present calculation. Collectively, these quantum chemica analyses substantiate that MTT can robustly adsorb onto the cathode surface during electroplating.

From the above analyses, MTT can spontaneously adsorb onto the cathode interface in the plating bath, while simultaneously interacting with bulk $\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 + }$ ions. To confirm the dominant role of interfacial adsorption, in situ FTIR spectra of the Cu working electrode were collected in VMS electrolyte containing 50 mg $\mathrm { L } ^ { - 1 }$ MTT at applied potentials ranging from −0.45 V to −0.65 V (vs SSE, 50 mV step). As shown in Figure S8, a series of vibrational features in the $1 0 0 0 { - } 1 7 0 0 \ \mathrm { ~ c m ^ { - 1 } }$ fingerprint region�attributable to the phenyl, tetrazolium, thiazole, and methyl moieties of MTT (phenyl and tetrazolium $\scriptstyle \mathrm { C = C / C = N }$ stretches near 1500− $1 6 2 0 ~ \mathrm { { c m } ^ { - 1 } }$ , thiazole/phenyl ring deformations near 1400− $1 5 0 0 ~ \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } .$ , methyl C−H bending near $1 3 8 0 { - } 1 4 1 0 ~ \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } , \mathrm { C } { - }$ N stretches near $1 2 7 0 { - } 1 3 3 0 ~ \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ , and ring-breathing modes near $1 0 4 0 { - } 1 1 5 0 \ \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$ �grow monotonically in intensity as the applied potential becomes more cathodic, providing direct in situ evidence for progressive MTT accumulation at the Cu cathode interface. Since the bulk cation−π interaction is much weaker than interfacial adsorption, it cannot appreciably hinder the difusion and subsequent adsorption of MTT at the cathode. Consequently, the overall inhibition eficiency is governed primarily by interfacial adsorption.

Based on the aforementioned theoretical calculations, topological analyses, and in situ FTIR spectroelectrochemical measurements, it can be concluded that the inhibition mechanism of MTT in the electrodeposition system arises from an asymmetric combination of two effects of markedly diferent magnitudes. At the cathode interface, MTT adsorbs strongly to form a dense blocking molecular layer that reduces the available active sites for $\mathrm { \Delta C u } ^ { 2 + }$ reduction (interfacial adsorption efect; the dominant kinetic contribution). In the bulk electrolyte, a small fraction of MTT engages $\dot { \mathrm { C u } } ^ { 2 + }$ ions through a comparatively weak cation−π interaction, modestly raising the activation barrier for ${ \mathrm { C u } } ^ { 2 + }$ reduction at the eventual interface (bulk cation−π contribution; a minor secondary efect).

To comprehensively evaluate the through-hole filling capability of MTT, the thickness uniformity of its electrodeposited copper layers within printed circuit board (PCB) throughholes was systematically characterized. In the PCB through hole electroplating process, Throwing Power (TP) serves as the pivotal quantitative index for evaluating the internal deposit thickness uniformity and evaluating the quality of the copper interconnects. The magnitude of the TP directly dictates the electrical reliability and long-term service lifespan of the 3D interconnected structures. Figures 5a,b, and S6 display high-resolution metallographic cross-sectional optical micrographs of the through-holes after electrodeposition under various MTT concentrations. At a constant current density of $2 \mathrm { A } / \mathrm { d } \mathrm { m } ^ { 2 } ,$ when VMS exclusively contains the accelerator SPS and the suppressor PEG (Figure 5a), the TP value of the through-hole is only 25.2%. At this juncture, a distinct geometric disparity exists between the deposit thickness at the opening and that in the central region, resulting in a severe “dog-bone” morphological defect that fundamentally fails to meet the electrical reliability requirements for high-density interconnects. Remarkably, with the introduction of MTT into the plating system, this geometric efect of uneven deposit distribution is efectively suppressed, and the overall coating morphology transits almost into a conformal deposition. As illustrated in Figure 5b, upon adding an optimal MTT concentration of 50 mg/L, the TP value increases to 96.8%. This visually dictates that MTT bridges the thickness gap between the surface opening and the deep interior, achieving high-quality conformal thickening of the copper layer within the through-hole.

To further benchmark the leveling performance of MTT against a well-established commercial leveler, a comparative through-hole electroplating experiment was conducted using 50 mg/L Janus Green B (JGB) under identical bath composition and process conditions. As illustrated in Figure S6d, the cross-sectional metallographic micrograph of the through-hole electroplated with JGB reveals a relatively uniform copper distribution along the hole wall, with no pronounced “dog-bone” defect observable at the orifice. Nevertheless, the overall copper deposit thickness within the through-hole remains noticeably thin compared to that achieved with MTT, yielding a TP value of approximately 84.5%. Although this TP value represents a substantial improvement over the additive-free system (TP = 25.2%), it remains significantly inferior to the 96.8% attained with 50 mg/L MTT. This performance disparity can be rationalized by the stronger cathodic polarization and more pronounced convection-dependent adsorption behavior of MTT, as demonstrated by the electrochemical analyses in Section 3.2. The higher inhibitory potency of MTT at the forcedconvection orifice region enables a more efective redistribution of the electric field lines toward the through-hole interior, thereby yielding superior thickness uniformity. These comparative results unequivocally corroborate the exceptional leveling eficacy of MTT and its marked advantage over the conventional JGB leveler in high-aspect-ratio through-hole electroplating applications.

Coupling the theoretical elucidation of the MTT inhibition mechanism in Section 3.3 with previous studies, competitive interfacial polarization remodeling driven by a multiphysics coupling mechanism was proposed to unveil the intrinsic influence of MTT. As portrayed in the schematic mechanism (Figure 5c), governed by the coupling of fluid dynamics (convective mass transfer) and electrochemical kinetics, MTT, PEG, and SPS undergo competitive adsorption at the solid− liquid interface within the through-hole. This induces a spatially diferentiated distribution of polarization resistance, reshaping the potential field across the inner surface of the through-hole. Specifically, propelled by the forced convection at the hole opening, MTT rapidly accumulates and adsorbs in this region via convection-dependent adsorption (CDA).<sup>54,55</sup> Concurrently, MTT interacts synergistically with the PEG polymer chains and the bridging chloride ions to form a dense ternary synergistic suppression film on the copper substrate. This compact adsorption layer triggers a notable increase in the local polarization resistance at the opening. The resulting elevated electrochemical reaction barrier efectively suppresses the electroreduction kinetics of ${ \mathrm { C u } } ^ { 2 + }$ in this vicinity. Consequently, the increased polarization resistance at the orifice compels the spatial electric field lines $( \mathrm { i . e . , }$ the primary current distribution) to redistribute toward the deep interior of the through-hole, which is situated in a weak convection zone.<sup>56,57</sup> Through this polarization remodeling efect, the inherent Ohmic potential drop caused by the geometric aspect ratio of the through-hole is compensated. Simultaneously, a steady-state difusion flux of $\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 + }$ directed into the hole is sustained, ultimately driving the realization of a conformal through-hole deposition.

In summary, this study systematically investigated the application performance and multiphysics coupling mechanisms of MTT, acting as a leveler for copper electrodeposition in PCB through-holes. Electrochemical evaluations demon strate that MTT significantly enhances cathodic polarization via a convection-dependent interfacial adsorption. Meanwhile, microscopic morphological characterization confirms that MTT exhibits excellent leveling capability, significantly reducing the surface roughness of the copper deposit to 0.147 μm. Such a smooth surface topography is highly beneficial for mitigating the skin efect and lowering insertion loss during high-frequency signal transmission. Density functional theory analysis further elucidates that the microscopic origin of this robust inhibitory behavior lies primarily in the strong interfacial adsorption of MTT at the cathode, with the bulk cation−π interaction with ${ \mathrm { C u } } ^ { 2 + }$ contributing as a minor secondary efect. Phase structure and interface analysis illustrate that an optimal MTT concentration (50 mg/L) not only efectively refines the crystalline grain size and promotes the preferential growth of the Cu(200) plane but also decreases the solid−liquid interfacial contact angle to ${ 5 4 . 6 } ^ { \circ } ,$ thereby fundamentally suppressing the generation of macroscopic morphological defects. Ultimately, in practical throughhole electroplating applications, the competitive adsorption among MTT, PEG, and SPS induces a spatially diferentiated remodeling of polarization resistance. By establishing a high impedance barrier at the forced-convection orifice region, the inherent Ohmic potential drop within the through-holes is efectively compensated. Driven by this multiphysical coupling mechanism, the TP value of through-holes is substantially elevated from 25.2% to 96.8%, markedly outperforming the conventional leveler JGB (TP = 84.5%) under identical conditions, successfully achieving high-quality conformal deposition and providing a theoretical and practical basis for the fabrication of highly reliable, high-frequency 3D interconnected PCB structures.

Additives are widely used to modulate the conditions of plating in electrodeposition. In particular, when performing feature filling, additives are essential components that cause a variation in the deposition speed depending on the deposition spots, thereby enabling the performance of superconformal filling. Copper bottom-up filling electrodeposition is performed using a threeadditive system consisting of a suppressor, an accelerator, and a leveler. Many studies have been conducted on the behavior of additives and their growth mechanisms; however, various additives are still being developed for copper electrodeposition.<sup>19–24</sup> I n the case of nickel, one of the iron group metals, there have also been many studies on additives for superconformal filling. Polyethyleneimine (PEI) and benzimidazole derivatives, such as 2-mercaptobenzimidazole (MBI) and 2-mercapto-5-benzimidazolesulfonic acid (MBIS), were shown to yield void-free feature filling.<sup>25–27</sup> Conversely, for cobalt, there are studies on the additives and mechanisms for cobalt bottom-up filling, although these are still insufficient. In cobalt bottom-up electrodeposition, some studies explain the mechanism based on the S-shaped negative differential resistance theory<sup>28,29</sup> and the deposition speed difference due to complex formation,<sup>30</sup> which has been suggested in copper bottom-up filling studies. Studies explaining the mechanism based on the interaction with the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) involved in cobalt reduction have also been reported.<sup>31,32</sup>

As is well known, HER inevitably occurs during cobalt electrodeposition, and one must be familiar with these secondary processes to understand cobalt electrodeposition. These secondary processes increase the pH at the electrode–electrolyte interface, and cobalt hydroxide may precipitate under the increased pH condition.<sup>33,34</sup> In this case, considerably large nodules and rough surfaces are formed and conductivity is reduced, resulting in a reduction in the quality of cobalt plating. To prevent this, boric acid with a buffering capability is mainly used in Watts-type plating baths.<sup>35,36</sup> Similarly, if an additive that can suppress the HER in the potential region of cobalt deposition is used, the current efficiency can be increased, and the quality of the plating can be improved by inhibiting the increase in pH. In this study, MBI was selected as an additive capable of bottom-up filling by suppressing this additional reaction and increasing the cobalt deposition overpotential.

随着集成电路的集成度越来越高，晶体管的尺寸已经达到纳米级别。在 14nm 节点下，由于尺寸效应的影响，Cu 互连线的电阻率呈现指数级升高，需要新的材料替代部分金属 Cu 作为互连线。金属 Co 因其电子平均自由程较短，电阻率低，性能稳定和较低的电迁移能引起广泛关注。但是，由于新型芯片技术的发展时间短和工艺技术不成熟，对于适合金属 Co 填充过程的抑制剂结构以及抑制剂的分子结构仍需要进一步分析研究。因此，研究无缝填充 Co 技术具有非常重要的理论和实际价值。本论文首先通过理论计算和赫尔槽实验，对比了不同结构的添加剂对 Co 镀液的分散能力，确定了适合作为抑制剂的分子结构，并对抑制剂在镀液中的电化学行为以及填充效果进行了探讨，最终确定了适合微米级别盲孔填充的金属 Co 电镀工艺。

通过赫尔槽实验分析了 14 种不同结构的添加剂分子对 Co 沉积过程的影响，发现 C=N 环己二烯共轭结构和四氮唑共轭结构的分子可以提高 Co 镀液的分散能力。通过填充效果对比，发现具有共轭结构的孔雀石绿（MG）和氯化硝基四氮唑蓝（NBT）分别作为添加剂时，明显抑制 Co 在盲孔外表面的沉积速率，但是对盲孔底部沉积速率抑制效果不明显。通过分子动力学（MD）模拟分析，发现 MG 分子内的特殊 C=N 环己二烯共轭结构，可以有效地吸附在阴极表面，占据活性位点，阻碍 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 沉积。同时，NBT 分子内的四氮唑共轭结构也同样容易吸附在阴极表面，而且相较于 MG，NBT 具有更高的吸附能。

通过镀液的电化学测试得知，较低浓度的 MG 和 NBT 就使 Co 还原电位发生明显的负移，而且随着抑制剂浓度的增加，镀液的极化过电位增加。通过计时电流曲线得出，增加镀液的传质速度，Co 的极化过电位增加，说明抑制剂 MG和 NBT 在阴极表面的吸附过程受传质过程控制。利用电化学石英晶体微天平（EQCM）测试发现，MG 和 NBT 作为抑制剂时，吸附在阴极表面阻碍 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 沉积，降低了沉积效率。通过与伏安曲线对比分析得出，MG 和 NBT 不仅抑制了Co 还原过程，还促进了氢还原过程。用同摩尔量的 K<sup>+</sup>代替 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 并进行循环伏安测试发现，MG 和 NBT 促进了析氢反应（HER），从而导致镀液的 pH 值升高。结合理论分析得知，抑制剂分子吸附在阴极表面，占据活性位点，阻碍 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 成核沉积；吸附在阴极表面的添加剂分子充当 HER 的活性位点，促进氢析出。通过 Co 还原电流和镀液还原的总电流对比得知，尽管镀液中有硼酸的存在，但是添加剂促进了 $_ { \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } }$ 的还原过程，导致局部 pH 值升高。

通过填充过程分析得知，MG 和 NBT 具有较强的抑制能力。添加低浓度的MG 和 NBT 于镀液中进行填充发现，盲孔底部的沉积速率高于外表面。对比不同电势下的填充效果分析得知，抑制剂在-1.20V 沉积电势下的填充机理和-1.25V 时不同，较低沉积电势下，镀液主要发生氢还原过程，由此引起的 pH 值升高在盲孔底部对流速率慢的区域更加明显，使底部具有更高的沉积速率。在-1.25V 沉积电势下，底部镀层的沉积速率差不多是外表面的 2 倍，使微米级别盲孔$( 1 0 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { m } \times 1 0 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { m } )$ 的填充率 FR 值分别达到 72.6%和 84.5%。而在-1.20 V 时，其 FR 值分别达到 90.3%和 91.9%。最终筛选出适合盲孔填充的最优配方分别是0.4 mol/L $\mathrm { C o S O _ { 4 } }$ ，0.5 mol/L $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ ，10 mmol/L NaCl，20 mg/L MPS，10 mg/LMG 和 0.4 mol/L $\mathrm { C o S O _ { 4 } }$ ，0.5 mol/L $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ ，10 mmol/L NaCl，20 mg/L NBT。对比不同沉积时间的填充图发现，低电势下，盲孔内形成的活化-钝化区域更明显，更有利于实现金属 $\mathrm { C o }$ 的无缝填充。最终根据添加剂这一作用机理，提出吸附-诱导-扩散填充机理，即抑制剂吸附在阴极表面抑制 Co 沉积；抑制剂诱导氢析出，导致局部 $\mathsf { p H }$ 值升高，底部容易形成氢氧化钴中间态，提高底部沉积速率；由于抑制剂受扩散控制，容易在盲孔形成抑制梯度，从而实现自底而上的无缝Co 填充。
关键词: 孔雀石绿；氯化硝基四氮唑蓝；抑制剂；Co 填充；氢析出；吸附-诱导-扩散机理

With the increasing integration of integrated circuits, the size of transistors has reached the nm level. Due to the influence of size effect, the resistivity of Cu interconnectors increases exponentially when the line width below 14 nm. So new materials are needed to replace metal Cu as interconnects. Metal Co has attracted widespread attention because of its short mean free path of electrons, low resistivity, stable performance and low electromigration. However, due to the short development time of the new chip technology and the immature process of new alternative materials, further analysis and study of the inhibitor and the molecular structure of the inhibitor suitable for the metal Co filling process are still needed. Therefore, studying the seamless filling Co technology has very important theoretical and practical value. According to theoretical calculation and Hull cell experiment, this paper compared the dispersion ability of plating bath after adding additives with different structures and their inhibition ability on Co plating bath, determined the molecular structure suitable for use as a Co plating inhibitor, and discussed the electrochemical behavior and filling effect of the inhibitor in the plating solution. Finally, a metal Co plating process suitable for micron level blind hole filling was verified.

The effect of 14 kinds of different additive molecules on Co deposition process was analyzed through Hull cell experiment. It was found that molecular with C=N cyclohexadiene conjugated structure and tetrazole conjugated structure can improve the dispersion ability of Co plating solution. By comparing the filling process, Malachite Green (MG) and Nitro Blue Tetrazolium Chloride (NBT) of the two conjugated structures were used as additives, the deposition rate of Co on the outer surface of the blind hole was significantly inhibited, but the deposition rate at the bottom of the blind hole was not significantly inhibited. According to MD simulation analysis, the special C=N cyclohexadiene conjugated structure in MG molecules could be adsorbed on the cathode surface effectively, occupying the active site and preventing the deposition of $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ . While the conjugated structure of tetrazole in NBT molecule is also easy to be adsorbed on the cathode surface, and NBT has higher adsorption energy than MG.

The electrochemistry test of the plating solution showed that lower concentrations of MG and NBT (5 mg/L) caused a significant negative shift in the Co reduction potential, and with the increase in inhibitor concentration, the polarization overpotential of the plating solution increased. According to the chronoamperometric curve, increasing the mass transfer rate of the plating solution increases the polarization overpotential of Co, indicating that the adsorption process of inhibitors MG and NBT on the cathode surface is controlled by the mass transfer process. Electrochemical Quartz Crystal Microbalance (EQCM) testing showed that MG and NBT adsorbed on the cathode surface as inhibitors, which hindered the deposition of $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ and reduced the deposition efficiency. Compared with LSV curves, MG and NBT not only inhibited the Co reduction process, but also promoted the hydrogen reduction process. Cyclic voltammetry tests with $\mathrm { K } ^ { + }$ to replace $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ showed that MG and NBT promote the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in an increase of pH value in the plating solution. Based on theoretical analysis, it is known that inhibitor molecules adsorb on the cathode surface, occupying active sites, and hindering the nucleation and deposition of $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ ; The additive molecules adsorbed on the cathode surface act as active sites for HER, promoting hydrogen precipitation. By comparing the Co reduction current with the total current of the plating solution reduction, the additive promotes the reduction process of $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O }$ and resulting in a local pH increase, although there is boric acid in the plating solution.

According to the filling process analysis, MG and NBT have strong inhibition ability. When 10mg/L MG and NBT are added, the coating deposition rate at the bottom is higher than that at the surface under different voltages. According to the filling effect analysis, the filling mechanism of inhibitor at -1.20 V deposition voltage is different from that at -1.25 V deposition voltage. The plating solution mainly occurs hydrogen reduction process, the increase of pH value causes the higher deposition rate at the bottom is more obvious, obtained. At -1.25 V deposition voltage, the plating rate of the bottom deposition is nearly twice that of the outer surface. When MG and NBT are used as additives, the filling FR value of the micron pore reaches 72.6% and 84.5%, respectively. At -1.20 V, the FR values reached 90.3% and 91.9%, respectively. The optimal formulations were 0.4 mol/L $\mathrm { C o S O } _ { 4 } , 0 . 5$ mol/L $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 } .$ , 10 mmol/L NaCl, 20 mg/L MPS, 10 mg/L MG and 0.4 mol/L $\mathrm { C o S O } _ { 4 } , 0 . 5$ mol/L $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 10 mmol/L NaCl, 20 mg/L NBT, respectively. Compared with the filling conditions of different deposition times, the activation-passivation zone formed in the blind hole is more obvious under low voltage, which is more conducive to the realization of metal Co superfilling. Finally, according to the action mechanism of additives, the adsorption-induction-diffusion filling mechanism was proposed, that is, the inhibitor was adsorbed on the cathode surface to inhibit Co deposition. Inhibitor induced hydrogen precipitation, resulting in the increase of pH, the formation of cobalt hydroxide at the bottom of the intermediate state, improve the bottom deposition rate; Because the inhibitor is controlled by diffusion, it is easy to form an inhibition gradient in the blind hole, thus achieving seamless bottom-up Co filling

由于集成电路内三极管的制备用的是光刻技术，因此布线过程其实就是将金属材料沉积在盲孔或沟槽内实现无缝填充，而目前采用的工艺是电沉积工艺。自从大马士革铜互连工艺开发出来以后，电镀 Cu 技术一直是芯片布线的主要方式。之所以选择电沉积技术是因为只需要在镀液中添加少量的添加剂就能实现无缝填充，过程简单，操作便捷，商业价值高。也因此对于大马士革铜互连工艺的研究主要集中选择合适的添加剂实现金属 Cu 的高效无缝填充，其中添加剂的研究主要集中在加速剂、抑制剂和整平剂的筛选。

金属 Co 具有较低的平均电子自由程，因此作为纳米级别的互连线时，相较于体电阻率，其变化较小。作为互连材料，Co 仅需要一层阻抗层，而 Cu 则需要更厚的阻抗层和粘附层。此外，Co 的抗电迁移性能也比 Cu 更优异，因此作为替代材料，Co 在纳米级别互连中更具有优势，可以作为互连材料代替 Cu。对于 Co 的制备过程，仍以电沉积为主，这是因为只需要添加少量的抑制剂就可以实现 Co的无缝填充，因此对于添加剂的研究和选择也是目前的研究重点。

尽管目前有一些关于金属 Co 填充过程中的添加剂的研究，但是对于如何选择以及选择何种结构的添加剂，仍没有定论。而且文献中报道的抑制剂多为聚合物，这是基于长链结构容易在电极表面吸附，阻碍 Co 沉积，但同时又面临一个问题，Co 作为替代金属，主要用于纳米级别的互连的，而长链结构的大分子容易在孔口处堆叠致使沉积过程离子传输受阻，容易导致盲孔内出现缝隙。而小分子作为添加剂时，则需要较高的浓度以达到无缝填充的抑制效果，这种情况下容易导致 Co 镀层中出现 C，N 和 O 等原子掺杂，进而使 Co 镀层电阻率进一步升高，因此选择一种合适分子量的抑制剂也是提高 Co 镀层性能的关键。本文首先根据文献调研筛选了多种不同结构的添加剂作为抑制剂，研究其对 Co 填充过程影响，然后利用 MD 模拟和 QC 计算分析不同结构的添加剂，通过与实验测试对比分析适合 Co 填充的分子结构，从而确定合适的添加剂分子结构与模拟计算之间的关系，为以后在不同尺寸的盲孔或通孔进行填充时提供一种可用的添加剂筛选方案。此外，由于 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 还原过程中同时发生 HER，本文还研究了抑制剂对氢还原过程的影响，并通过电化学测试和填充实验分析了 HER 过程在填充过程中的作用，为以后 Co 在纳米级别盲孔中的填充过程提供了一种可用的机理模型。

但是，Al 互连线与 $\mathrm { S i O } _ { 2 }$ 结合性好，表面易钝化从而性能稳定，因此研究人员尝试引入合金来改善 Al 的电迁移现象<sup>[18-20]</sup>。于是，IBM 公司通过在 Al 线中掺杂 $1 \ \mathrm { a t . \% } \{ \sim 2 \ \mathrm { a t . \% } \ \mathrm { C u }$ 以提高互连线的抗电迁移能力<sup>[21]</sup>。通过对比发现，Cu 的电阻率 $1 . 7 { \sim } 1 . 9 ~ { \mu } \Omega { \cdot } { \mathrm { c m } }$ 低于 Al 的 $2 . 8 { \sim } 2 . 9 ~ { \mu } \Omega { \cdot } \mathrm { c m }$ ，而且 Cu 的抗电迁移能力也要高于 Al 互连材料。随后，研究人员开始选择 Cu 来替代 Al 作为互连线，但是采用 Al 的布线方式制备出的 Cu 线不容易被蚀刻<sup>[22]</sup>。

大马士革电镀铜工艺主要是利用不同添加剂的相互作用，使铜离子在盲孔内外沉积时出现镀速差，其经典的组成配方为：加速剂为双（硫丙基）二硫化物（SPS），整平剂为健那绿（JGB）以及抑制剂聚乙二醇（PEG）。基础镀液组成为 $\mathrm { C u S O _ { 4 } }$ 和 $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { S O } _ { 4 }$ 。在大规模集成电路中，镀液的配方往往采用低铜高酸的基础镀液和不同浓度的添加剂以达到无缝填充的效果<sup>[28]</sup>，作用机理如图 1-4。

如图 1-4 所示，抑制剂 PEG 与溶液中还原的 $\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 \cdot }$ 形成稳定 PEG-Cu(I)-Cl<sup>-</sup>配合物，从而抑制 Cu 成核沉积，但是随着沉积的进行，盲孔或沟槽外表面 PEG浓度变化不大，而底部 PEG 由于掺杂进镀层或被击穿导致浓度降低，此时 SPS吸附在底部阴极表面，逐渐分解为 MPS，然后与还原的一价 Cu 和 Cl<sup>-</sup>形成的MPS-Cu(I)-Cl<sup>-</sup>配合物吸附在阴极表面，其中 S 原子作为活性位点促进 Cu 成核沉积。而 JGB 整平剂被认为是吸附在开口处，从而使开口处的沉积过程延迟到最后的封孔<sup>[29]</sup>。在后续的发展中，大马士革镀铜工艺几乎一直按照这一机理进行，只是在研究过程中选择不同的可替换的添加剂来适应不同尺寸的盲孔或沟槽。

其次，自从化学镀 Co 被报道出来<sup>[65]</sup>，利用化学镀的方式同样可以实现 Co的填充过程。但是目前所报道的化学镀 Co 主要集中在将 Co 作为粘附层沉积在阻挡层 TaN 上，以提高 Cu 互连线的附着力<sup>[66-69]</sup>。相对于电镀的方式，化学镀可以在非导体的基底上沉积，因为在沉积过程中会在基底上首先吸附还原性的离子/原子，然后促使 Co 离子还原沉积<sup>[70-72]</sup>。但是，化学镀制备的 Cu 填充线，其在沟槽或通孔内的镀层厚度往往低于外表面的厚度，这种方式更适合制备粘附层或阻抗层。因此，如果通过化学镀的方法进行 Co 无缝填充时，还需要考虑添加剂与化学镀的还原剂之间的相互作用，添加剂的作用机理也更加复杂。此外，研究表明采用 ALD 的方法制备的单层 Ru 原子，可以作为互连材料的阻挡层<sup>[73,</sup> <sup>74]</sup>。因此，相较于化学镀的方式，利用电沉积的方法制备 Co 互连线更便捷（省去了还原/活化过程），操作流程更简单，更经济实用。所以本文通过在镀液中加入合适的抑制剂，利用电沉积的方式制备 Co 填充层。

Ho 等人<sup>[90]</sup>通过在 $\mathrm { C o S O _ { 4 } }$ 镀液中添加不同浓度的 $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 来研究其对 Co 纳米颗粒的影响发现， $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 的加入使 Co 还原和氢还原电势负移，而且还原电流减低，这要归因于 $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 可以吸附在阴极表面占据活性位点。通过 XRD 分析得知， $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 倾向于吸附在 Co 晶体的 hcp(1011)晶面，从而使 Co 晶体向hcp(1010)过渡，而且晶粒尺寸下降。随着晶面取向的变化，磁滞回线的矫顽力逐渐降低。Sivasubramanian 等人<sup>[91]</sup>在电沉积 Co 三维枝晶时发现， $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 在阴极表面吸附对 Co 沉积起到抑制作用，而且由于 Co 晶体的(111)晶面的能量最低，受抑制作用较小，从而制备出了三维枝晶。说明 $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 还有导向剂的作用，有利于制备单晶结构。Karwas 等人<sup>[92]</sup>在对 Co-Zn 合金沉积时发现， $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 可以对 Co 成核和生长速率有较大影响，这是因 $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 存在时可以增加 $\mathbf { C o }$ 的成核密度，从而进一步使晶粒细化。

当用 Watts 型镀液沉积 Co 时，Rigsby 等人<sup>[93]</sup>对于 $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 在 $\mathbf { C o }$ 填充过程的作用机理进行详细分析。 $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 的加入使 镀层的粗糙度降低，增加了 $\mathbf { C o }$ 的极化过电位。而且不同 $\mathrm { p H }$ 条件下， $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 的电离常数也发生变化，结合 XPS图谱分析， $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 镀液中的解离过程如式(1-1)到(1-5)所示。当 $\mathrm { H } _ { 3 } \mathrm { B O } _ { 3 }$ 浓度为10 g/L 时，镀液中主要以[B(OH)4]<sup>-</sup>的形态存在，而当浓度增加至 40 g/L 时，随着 $\mathrm { p H }$ 的升高，镀液中硼酸的多聚态增加，因此镀液中起主要缓冲作用的是硼酸的多聚态。而且这种多聚态化合物抑制氢还原过程，同时与 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 形成络合物影响 Co 的成核沉积过程，两种共同作用有利于实现 Co 在沟槽内的填充。
Jung 等人<sup>[96]</sup>通过对比不同 Cl<sup>-</sup>浓度对 Co 镀层腐蚀行为的影响发现，在碱性环境下 Cl<sup>-</sup>的加入可以有效的减少 Co 镀层的钝化过程，促进 Co 镀层还原，说明 Cl<sup>-</sup>的加入可以改善沉积时阳极 Co 的钝化过程。
综上所述，在 Co 镀液中 Cl<sup>-</sup>离子主要用于活化阳极，改善镀层形貌，因此在镀液中选择添加少量 Cl<sup>-</sup>。
## （2）电压依赖抑制效应

## （3）抑制氢还原机理

Kang 等人<sup>[110]</sup>利用 2-巯基苯并咪唑（MBI）作为抑制剂研究其对 Co 填充过程的影响发现，MBI 对 Co 还原和 HER 过程均有抑制作用，但是随着浓度的增加，对 Co 的抑制作用明显增强，但是却对 HER 过程的抑制作用不明显。在以氯化银电极为参比电极的情况下，通过不同电势下的填充效果对比发现，当 MBI 的浓度达到 150μmol/L 时，在-1.10V 时沟槽内镀层沉积速率高于外表面的沉积速率。通过对比不同转速下镀层的填充厚度发现，较低转速时，MBI对沟槽外表面的抑制效果不明显，当转速达到 500rpm 时，沟槽内沉积速度高于外表面，说明在 500rpm 时可以实现金属 Co 的超共形沉积。分析 MBI 的作用机理是 MBI 吸附在阴极表面阻碍 Co 还原和 HER 过程，MBI 在沟槽底部被击穿或消耗而浓度降低，抑制失效，同时 MBI 对 HER 的抑制作用提高了 Co沉积效率；沟槽的外表面在高速搅拌下，吸附的 MBI 浓度变化不大，对 Co 的抑制作用占主要，从而形成 V 型轮廓。
## （4）氢诱导抑制失效

Wu 等人<sup>[64]</sup>研究了抑制剂（XF）对金属 Co 填充过程的影响，通过与没有添加剂的基础镀液的 CV 曲线对比，加入抑制剂后镀液的 CV 曲线出现明显的滞后现象，如图 1-15 所示。通过改变 CV 扫描的终止电势发现，终止电势越大，回扫的滞后现象越明显，说明 XF 的抑制效果是渐进的失效过程。对比不同 pH 下的 CV 曲线，较低过电势下，较高的 H<sup>+</sup>使抑制剂变为了加速剂，而较高过电势，抑制剂效果明显，说明 H<sup>+</sup>还原过程参与了抑制剂的失效反应。
因此，文献中认为这种抑制剂 可以与原子 反应，使抑制失效。通过填充实验，提出氢诱导失活机理，即沟槽内填充 时， 的抑制作用使沟槽外 Co 沉积过程受到抑制，沟槽内由于传质过程的影响和氢诱导的失活效应促使底部沉积效率较高，从而实现了金属 的超填充过程。

Rigsby 等人<sup>[111]</sup>选择 Watts 型镀液中添加抑制剂研究了 pH 值的变化对 Co填充过程的影响。通过 EQCM 与 CV 曲线对比发现，Co 沉积过程中首先发生H<sup>+</sup>还原，然后是 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 还原，当添加合适的抑制剂时，使 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 与 $_ { \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } }$ 同时还原。

在此过程中可能会形成氢氧化钴产物，如图 1-16 所示。通过 EQCM 曲线外推计算的 Tafel 斜率证实，OH<sup>-</sup>参与了 Co 还原过程。计算不同搅拌速度和不同 pH值条件下的沉积效率得出，pH 值的增加有利于 Co 沉积，而且受传质过程的影响。因此，认为在 Co 还原过程中形成了 $\mathrm { C o ( O H ) ^ { + } }$ 中间态。他提出 pH 值驱动机理，Co 在填充过程由于沟槽外部受抑制剂作用，沉积效率低，镀速慢；而底部由于 HER 过程，导致 pH 值出现局部升高，出现的 OH<sup>-</sup>可以与 $\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 + }$ 形成 Co(OH)<sup>+</sup>中间态，这种中间态吸附在底部，取代开始时吸附的抑制剂，使抑制失效，促进底部 Co 沉积，从而形成沟槽内外的沉积速率梯度，实现了 Co 的超填充。

国内的何为组<sup>[112,</sup> <sup>113]</sup>研究了 3-巯基丙烷磺酸钠（MPS）和聚乙烯吡咯烷酮（PVP）这两种添加剂对 Co 填充过程的机理，通过 CV 曲线发现低浓度的 MPS对 Co 还原过程有加速作用，而 PVP 对 Co 还原有抑制作用。通过量子化学计算发现 MPS 和 PVP 的 $E _ { \mathrm { g } }$ 能级相近，MPS 中处于 HOMO 能级的磺酸基团可以作为吸附的活性位点，而且 PVP 内的酰胺基团静电势较高可以吸附在电极表面。提出竞争吸附的机理，较高浓度的 PVP 可以有效的抑制 Co 在沟槽内沉积，而随着底部 PVP 的消耗，MPS 逐渐取代吸附的 PVP，占据活性位点促使$\mathrm { C o } ^ { 2 \dag }$ 还原沉积；外表面较高浓度的 PVP 仍然吸附在表面，抑制 Co 成核沉积，从而形成内外的镀速差，实现了沟槽的无缝填充。

根据以上研究，抑制剂是实现金属 Co 填充的关键，抑制能力的大小主要取决于内部的官能团。但是，对于越来越小的晶体管（10 nm 以下），需要 Co填充的沟槽或盲孔的尺寸更加精细。当聚合物作为抑制剂时，容易吸附在盲孔开口处堵塞内部离子传输过程。这是由于聚合物型抑制剂自身的聚合度决定的，因此在 nm 级别的沟槽或盲孔填充时，不适合选择聚合物型抑制剂。而小分子的抑制剂抑制能力较弱，需要添加高浓度的小分子作为抑制剂，容易造成 Co镀层内 C，N 和 O 等杂质原子的含量较高，从而影响其电迁移和电阻率。因此，本文将重点研究抑制能力强的大分子抑制剂。

Wang 等人<sup>[120]</sup>利用 MD 模拟预测和分析了 N-丁基-N-甲基哌啶溴盐$( \mathrm { P P } _ { 1 4 } \mathrm { B r } )$ 在 Cu 的通孔电镀中的作用，经过计算得出其在 Cu(001)晶面的吸附能达到 197.8 kJ/mol，由此得出，较高吸附能的添加剂可以有效的抑制金属离子在阴极表面的沉积过程。而且通过通孔测试发现这种添加剂可以作为整平剂吸附在通孔开口处，抑制开口处 Cu 的沉积速率，也印证了 MD 模拟的结果。Zhou 等人<sup>[121]</sup>利用 MD 模拟分析 5-氨基-1,3,4-噻二唑-2-硫醇在 Cu(111)晶面的上的吸附过程，最终计算得到吸附能为 34.6 kcal/mol，而且经过模拟之后，这种分子结构排列几乎与 Cu 基底平行，说明其可以很好的吸附在阴极表面，起到抑制效果，并通过填充实验进行了验证。Wu 等人<sup>[122]</sup>分析了十六烷基三甲基溴化铵（CTAB）在 Cu 填充中的抑制作用，通过 MD 模拟和填充测试结果分析发现，CTAB 可以有效的吸附在 Cu 表面，起到抑制 Cu 沉积的作用。Zheng等人<sup>[123]</sup>分析了1-乙烯基咪唑和1,4-丁二醇二缩水甘油醚的共聚物（VIBDGE）作为整平剂对金属 Cu 沉积的影响，通过 MD 模拟发现这种共聚物在 Cu 表面具有较大的吸附能 163.4 kcal/mol，与健那绿（JGB）相比，VIBDGE 的吸附能高于 PEG（149.2 kcal/mol）。
上述分析可知，MD 模拟可以作为对添加剂吸附能力的分析和预测，因此本文中根据文献调研和实验测试分析了不同结构添加剂的抑制能力，并根据MD 模拟过程对添加剂分子结构进行分析。

Yin等人<sup>[124]</sup>首先利用 MD模拟分析了苯并三唑(BTA)和 1,2,4-三氮唑(TAZ)在 Co 阴极表面的吸附情况，然后根据 QC 计算分析了两种抑制剂的抑制能力强弱。根据前沿分子轨道理论，E 能级值越高，分子内的电子更容易转移至能量较低空分子的轨道，同时能级差值∆E 越低，代表着分子活性越高，抑制能力越强。根据计算结果得出 BTA $( E _ { \mathrm { H O M O } } { = } { - } 5 . 8 9 8 \ \mathrm { e V } , \Delta \mathrm { E = } 3 . 7 9 7 \ \mathrm { e V } )$ 的抑制能力明显强于 TAZ $( E _ { \mathrm { H O M O } } { = } { - } 6 . 4 4 6 \ \mathrm { e V } , \Delta \mathrm { E } = 5 . 4 2 1 \ \mathrm { e V } )$ ，并与阻抗谱实验测试得到的结果相一致。Zhang 等人<sup>[125]</sup>选择了氨基乙酸(Gly)和 3-巯基 1-丙烷磺酸钠(MPS)作为电镀钴的添加剂，利用 QC 计算对比两种添加剂分子结构发现，相较于 Gly，MPS 具有更低的 $E _ { \mathrm { H O M O } }$ 能级值，但是两者的∆E 相近。然后通过分子静电势计算发现，MPS 的表面经典势高于 Gly，所以 MPS 更容易吸附在阴极表面，MPS 和 Gly 存在竞争吸附的关系。
由上述可知，QC 计算可以被用来分析计算添加剂分子的前沿分子轨道信息，并模拟分析出可能产生吸附作用的官能团和起到抑制作用的结构，有利于从分子层面对添加剂进行详细分析，并且还可以根据计算结果推测和改进添加剂的结构。

（2）电镀 Co 互连工艺由于发展时间短，对于添加剂的选择以及添加剂分子结构组成并没有详细研究。而且对于添加剂，目前研究主要集中在抑制剂的选择，添加剂分子中的 C=N 被认为是起到抑制的关键，但是对于其作用过程以及机理分析仍然不明确。根据最新研究表明，Co 的合金（CoAl 等）在抗电迁移<sup>[54]</sup>性能中表现优异，因此在未来的芯片互连中 Co 合金或金属间化合物或许也可以作为 Cu 替代材料，对于抑制剂的筛选将更加复杂。

（3）由于尺寸效应的影响，添加剂尤其是小分子的添加剂在沉积过程中掺杂到 相中，出现 ， ， ， 和 等原子掺杂，杂原子对于 的电阻率和电迁移的影响目前仍需要进一步分析验证。而对于分子量较大的聚合物类抑制剂，根据量子化学计算发现其容易发生团聚形成较大直径的聚合物球<sup>[126]</sup>，而且随着分子量的增加其直径逐渐变大，由此引发的纳米级别盲孔孔口处聚集，导致填充时形成缝隙。因此，对于添加剂的分子量和盲孔尺寸之间的关系在实际填充中也需要进一步验证。
根据互连技术背景的分析研究，利用电沉积制备 Co 互连代替部分布线工艺的 Cu 互连是可行的，而且无论选择单金属还是合金作为替代材料，电镀工艺都是方便实用，便捷高效的方式，因此对于适合金属 Co 填充的抑制剂进行研究具有重要意义。此外，由上述总结分析，将理论计算用于对抑制剂内的分子结构的分析和验证是切实可行的，因此本论文的主要研究内容如下：

（ ）根据文献调研和总结选择多种不同分子结构的抑制剂，通过镀层表面形貌和镀液的赫尔槽实验，考察这些抑制剂对金属 Co镀液分散能力的影响。通过电化学测试和填充效果分析抑制剂的作用过程以及适合作为 填充的抑制剂结构。利用 MD 模拟考察抑制剂分子在阴极表面的吸附能，探究抑制剂的吸附关系和填充中抑制能力之间的联系，并通过 QC 计算探究抑制剂的内部分子结构并研究抑制剂的前沿分子轨道信息。根据理论和实验对比分析筛选出适合微米级别盲孔填充的抑制剂，并对抑制剂在镀液中作用方式进行分析。

（ ）通过考察孔雀石绿（ ）对镀液的极化电流，阴极沉积效率，阻抗的变化，分析 MG 对金属 Co 电沉积过程的影响。通过研究不同沉积条件下填充过程的变化，探究抑制剂的作用机理，同时根据抑制剂添加之后的成核过程的变化，分析抑制剂对金属 Co 成核过程的变化。通过探究抑制剂对 HER 过程的影响，考察由于氢还原引起的 pH 升高对填充过程的作用，并结合不同 pH值条件下的填充过程对填充机理进行分析，确定出最佳的工艺参数，并对填充机理进行总结分析。
（3）通过考察不同浓度氯化硝基四氮唑蓝（NBT）和不同搅拌速度对镀液电化学行为的影响，分析 NBT 的抑制作用机理，探究 NBT 在金属 Co 成核过程中的作用以及对镀层形貌和晶相结构的影响。考察 NBT 对氢还原过程的影响并探究 NBT作为单一添加剂时金属 Co的填充机理。通过对比 MG和NBT两种抑制剂对镀层的影响，对抑制剂分子结构和作用机制进一步分析研究。

通过文献总结发现，实现金属在盲孔或通孔中共形沉积的关键是添加剂的选择。选择单一添加剂或混合添加剂使盲孔或通孔内外形成明显的沉积速率差异才能更有利于金属的无缝填充。在大马士革电镀铜工艺中，合适浓度的抑制剂-加速剂-整平剂的相互作用，实现了金属铜在 TSV 中自底而上的填充。而选择“Watts”型镀钴液进行填充过程的研究时，镀液本身就有较高的极化过电位，具有一定的整平能力，因此在添加剂选择时往往是抑制剂或抑制剂-加速剂的选择。金属钴在芯片中应用时，由于具有较低的电子平均自由程，往往被用在14nm 以下的制程中作为互连材料。在此尺寸下，填充过程耗时很短，镀速较快，因此加速剂的作用就没有抑制剂的作用明显。此外，钴还原过程中伴随着氢还原过程，在研究钴沉积过程中还需要考虑氢还原的影响。

本章根据文献调研和总结选择了 14 种添加剂，其中柠檬酸<sup>[129]</sup>，香豆素<sup>[130,131]</sup>，香草醛<sup>[132-134]</sup>都在钴沉积中被认为具有整平作用，增加了钴阴极极化，但是在 Co 填充中很少被研究；吡啶-(2-偶氮-4)间苯二酚<sup>[135-138]</sup>，吉氏色素<sup>[139]</sup>作为添加剂时，可以吸附在钴离子表面或与钴形成稳定络合物，从而改变钴离子还原过程，但是对于钴填充过程影响需要进一步研究；结晶紫<sup>[140,</sup> <sup>141]</sup>，碱性品红<sup>[142]</sup>与臧红 T<sup>[143]</sup>作为颜料可以很好的吸附在阴极表面，而且作为添加剂可以吸附在阴极表面对金属离子沉积起到抑制作用，已经在铜填充过程作为了整平剂<sup>[144,145]</sup>，因此选择与其相似结构的碱性蓝、孔雀石绿作为添加剂进一步研究对钴填充影响。此外，具有四氮唑结构的分子在铜沉积中被认为具有较大的抑制作用<sup>[146-148]</sup>，可以作为整平剂有效的提高铜填充效果<sup>[149,</sup> <sup>150]</sup>，而且具有这种共轭结构的分子被认为可以发生开环反应，从而与金属离子形成稳定的络合物或螯合物<sup>[88]</sup>，从而对金属离子电化学行为产生较大影响，但是对于钴填充过程的影响并未被提及，因此在本章中选择了这十四种可能对金属钴沉积过程有作用的添加剂分子进行研究，

从图(a)中可以看出在没有添加任何添加剂时，镀层中出现大量的针脊状晶粒，而且镀层表面致密无针孔；(b-d)为添加含有碳基基团的柠檬酸，香豆素和香兰素后的镀层形貌，可以发现，镀层晶粒逐渐细化，而这种作用更多是归因于它们可以与镀液中的钴离子形成配合物，这种配合物可以抑制钴离子沉积过程，导致阴极极化增大，从而使晶粒细化；图(e-g)是添加具有 N=N 双键和吩噻嗪构型的添加剂后镀层的形貌，发现针脊状晶粒几乎消失，而且镀层晶粒变小。但是其中又有些许不同， 吡啶偶氮 间苯二酚为添加剂时，镀层中形成的镀层为不均匀块状晶粒；添加吉氏色素时晶粒为网状无定型形貌；镀液中添加中性红后，镀层变成大小较为均匀的块状晶粒。这同样应该归结为添加剂分子吸附在钴离子表面，影响钴离子还原过程，但是由于内部结构的不同导致形貌出现变化；图(h-l)是三苯甲烷类颜料为添加剂时的镀层形貌，可以看出由于内部结构不同，镀层形貌出现变化，总体上镀层的晶粒变小，其中（i 和k）镀层中出现针孔，k 图中针孔更小而且密集，这是因为氢析出造成的。藏花红 T 作为添加剂时，镀层变化较大，由最初的针脊状变为棒状，这或许与其在Co 成核时产生的晶面特定吸附有关<sup>[143]</sup>。通过图中也可以看出三苯甲烷类添加剂由于都是阳离子性分子，阴离子都是氯，具有较好可溶性，而且容易吸附在阴极表面，阻碍钴离子还原沉积，使钴镀层晶粒细化；图(m-o)中是氮杂环结构的分子加入后镀层的表面形貌，可以看出三氮唑和四氮唑结构的添加剂同样使晶粒细化，但是镀层形貌变化不大，仍然有少量针脊状晶粒出现。其中图（m）中凹凸不平的是基底形貌，可能是苯骈三氮唑作为添加剂时，抑制能力较强，在-1.30V 时，Co 沉积过程受抑制程度较大，镀层沉积较少。
从图 3-2 可以看出，添加剂均能使镀层晶粒细化，说明这些添加剂对钴离子沉积过程有抑制或细化晶粒的作用。那么，是否适合作为抑制剂实现金属钴的填充过程仍需要进一步研究。

作为可以实现金属钴填充的抑制剂，其根本是抑制剂分子优先吸附在高电流密度区域，抑制此区域内 Co 沉积过程，从而使钴离子在低电流密度区域同样可以沉积，也就是要具有整平作用，因此接下来通过赫尔槽实验研究添加剂分子对 Co 的整平效果，如图 3-3 所示。图 3-3(a)是没有任何添加剂的“Watts”型基础镀液，溶液 pH=4，温度为室温，采用磁力搅拌 1000rpm。电源选择 0.5A 的输出电流，赫尔槽体积为 267ml，黄铜板为负极，纯钴板为正极，电沉积时间为 5 min。

从图 3-3（a）中可以看出，由基础镀液制备的镀层在较高电流密度区域（红线左侧），镀层均匀平整，在较低电流密度区域（红线右侧），无沉积层，说明基础镀液在较低电流密度范围沉积不均匀。在图(b-d)中，高电流密度区域镀层均匀，而在较低电流密度区域无镀层，通过对比发现，三种添加剂使镀液制备的镀层面积呈增长趋势，柠檬酸<香豆素<香草醛。其中，香草醛电流密度范围与无添加剂时镀层几乎一样，说明这三种羰基官能团的添加剂在浓度为 20μmol/L 条件下，对钴离子沉积没有整平作用。尽管通过 SEM 图发现添加剂可以使 镀层晶粒细化，但是通过赫尔槽试片发现，对镀层没有整平效果，说明此浓度下，添加剂的抑制能力不明显，没有提高镀液的分散能力；图(e-g)中，添加 吡啶偶氮 间苯二酚和中性红后的赫尔槽试片照片，与无添加剂时相比，镀层范围几乎没有变化，说明此浓度下这两种添加剂没有改变镀液的分散能力。而吉氏色素的镀层范围变大，但是在高电流密度区域的镀层出现烧焦，翘曲。说明此浓度下吉氏色素在低电流区域抑制 Co 沉积，但是在较高电流区域有加速沉积的作用，添加剂在高电流密度区域容易失效。

图 3-3(h-l)中，镀液中添加三苯甲烷类的分子时发现，由于相邻苯环上取代基的不同，Co 沉积层覆盖范围出现明显差异其中以孔雀石绿镀层分布最为广泛，在 0.5A 电流下实现了镀层的完全覆盖，说明孔雀石绿具有很好的整平效果。对比图(k 和 l)发现，孔雀石绿和甲基紫均增加了镀层面积，说明这两种添加剂均对金属 Co 沉积有整平作用。根据其结构组成发现，这两种分子有相似的结构，都是 C=N 和环己二烯共轭结构，说明这种结构适合作为抑制剂。而通过与图(h 和 i)对比发现，碱性品红中苯环上的取代基换成 ${ \mathrm { - N H } } _ { 2 }$ 基之后，分子几乎没有抑制效果；而碱性蓝分子中的苯环上由于有 Cl 取代基，添加剂的整平能力同样减弱。图（i）中碱性蓝作为添加剂时，镀层光亮性明显优于无添加时的镀层，说明碱性蓝可以作为光亮剂，但是抑制能力并没有增强。
